context.whatBusinessDoes:
Northwind distributes industrial components to trade customers across the UK and Ireland. Customers hold credit accounts, place orders through reps or the trade counter, and are invoiced monthly. Sales operations manage pricing agreements per account; credit control releases or holds orders based on exposure.

The order-to-cash process is currently split across a legacy ERP and a set of spreadsheets, so order approval depends on one team's working knowledge rather than recorded rules.

scope.inScope: Order capture, approval and credit release
scope.reason: Owned by the 3PL under a separate contract
Different value stream, no overlap in objects

outcomes.outcome: Remove manual credit checks for low-risk orders

glossary.definition: A credit relationship with a trade customer, against which orders are placed and invoiced.
glossary.notConfuse: Contact — a person at the account

glossary.definition: A customer's committed request for goods at agreed prices.
The decision that an order may proceed given the account's current exposure.
glossary.notConfuse: Order approval — commercial sign-off on discount

objects.name: Account
objects.description: A trade customer's credit relationship with Northwind. An Account comes into existence when credit control approves an application, and stays live until it is closed or dormant for 24 months. Everything the business prices, invoices and chases hangs off the Account rather than the individual person placing an order.

properties.name: currentExposure
properties.description: Unpaid invoices plus released, uninvoiced orders

rules.rule: An Account on hold cannot have orders released.
rules.consequence: Order stays Awaiting credit; credit control notified

questions.question: Do group accounts share a single credit limit or one per subsidiary?

objects.example:
accountNumber: ACC-01882
tradingName: Hallam Engineering
creditLimit: 25000.00 GBP
currentExposure: 18420.00 GBP
status: Active

objects.name: Order
objects.description: A customer's committed request for goods at agreed prices. An Order exists from the moment a rep or the trade counter confirms the customer wants the goods, and stops mattering once it is fully invoiced or cancelled. It is the unit the business plans fulfilment and revenue around.

properties.name: totalValue
properties.description: Sum of line values excluding VAT

properties.name: discountPercent
properties.description: Discount applied beyond the account's agreement

properties.name: status
properties.description: Where the order is in its lifecycle

rules.rule: An Order cannot leave Draft without at least one line.
Discount above 10% requires commercial approval before credit release.

objects.example:
orderNumber: ORD-10023
accountNumber: ACC-01882   # LNK-01
placedAt: 2026-03-04T09:12Z
totalValue: 1420.00 GBP
discountPercent: 5
status: Awaiting credit

objects.name: OrderLine
objects.description: One product at one price and quantity within an Order. Lines exist only as part of an Order and are the level at which pricing agreements and stock allocation apply.

links.lifecycle: An Order cannot exist without an Account
links.why: Drives pricing, credit exposure and invoicing
links.mutable: An Order may be reassigned to another Account before release only
links.onDelete: Accounts are never deleted, only closed; orders are retained

links.lifecycle: Lines are cancelled with their Order
links.why: Line values roll up to order value and credit exposure

actions.name: CreateOrder
actions.pre: Account status is Active; at least one line added
actions.post: Order exists in Awaiting credit; exposure recalculated
actions.description: Captures a customer's commitment to buy at agreed prices, so fulfilment and credit can act on it.
actions.linksChanged: LNK-01 Account places Order; LNK-02 Order contains OrderLine
actions.reversible: Yes — via ACT-04 CancelOrder while not invoiced
actions.steps:
Select the account and confirm it is active
Add lines, applying the account's pricing agreement
Commit the order

failures.handling: Order saved as Draft; credit control notified
Routed to ACT-02 before credit release

actions.acceptance:
Given an active account with a pricing agreement, when a rep commits an order with two lines, then the order is Awaiting credit and its value equals the sum of line values
Given an account on hold, when a rep commits an order, then the order stays Draft and credit control is notified

actions.name: ReleaseOrderForFulfilment
actions.actor: Credit Controller, or the system when auto-release rules are met
actions.pre: Order is Awaiting credit; account is Active; exposure plus order value is within credit limit
actions.post: Order is Released; account exposure includes the order (supports O1 and O2)
actions.description: Decides whether an order may proceed given the account's current exposure — today a manual check on every order, which is what O2 targets.
actions.reversible: Yes — via ACT-06 PlaceAccountOnHold, which re-holds unfulfilled orders
actions.audit: Decision, decider, exposure at the time — 7 years
actions.steps:
Recalculate account exposure
Compare exposure plus order value against the credit limit
Release, or hold and notify the rep

failures.condition: Exposure plus order value exceeds the limit
failures.handling: Order held; credit control and rep notified with the shortfall

actions.acceptance:
Given an active account £5,000 below its limit, when a £2,000 order is released, then exposure increases by £2,000 and the order is Released
Given an account on hold, when release is attempted, then the order stays Awaiting credit

events.name: OrderReleased
events.carries: Order ID, account, value, decided by, timestamp

roles.description: Field sales, owns a set of accounts
roles.constraints: Own accounts only; discount capped at 10%

systems.notes: No outbound events today — a constraint on O1
